newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian PM warns diplomats of Khmer Rouge spies.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian PM warns diplomats of Khmer Rouge spies.

text.p: Cambodian Co-Premier Hun Sen said on Monday 80 Khmer Rouge spies had defected to the government in this southwest district and warned that a larger spy network threatened the country and diplomatic missions.
"The underground Khmer Rouge are a real security threat," said Hun Sen, speaking at a ceremony where the 80 suspected spies, dressed in civilian clothes, turned in 79 weapons.

"For us, this is a big problem. There are only 80 people and 79 (weapons) in one small district here, and there are 150 districts in the country," he told diplomats and journalists at Kong Pisey in Kompong Speu province, about 60 km (40 miles) southwest of Phnom Penh.
Hun Sen told the diplomats, including the U.S., British, Australian, Chinese, Vietnamese and Japanese envoys present, that spies could threaten their embassies.

"You stay in a big house with air conditioning, but our people are always threatened, every day. This is not a slingshot, this is a real B40. With three shots, it could destroy your embassy," he said, pointing a B40 rocket launcher and other confiscated weapons.
Hun Sen's comments came a week after he warned the U.S. ambassador to Cambodia, Kenneth Quinn, of unspecified espionage activities that could threaten foreign embassies.
The warning was passed on to other diplomats, and Hun Sen told Reuters he had stepped up security around foreign missions.
The Khmer Rouge, who led the brutal 1975-1979 "killing fields" regime during which more than a million Cambodians were killed, have been hit by thousands of defections in recent months.
Only about 800 to 2,000 hardliners are estimated to remain, mostly in the rebel stronghold of Anlong Veng, near the Thai border.
The Khmer Rouge reneged on a 1991 U.N.-sponsored peace pact and have been waging war against the government ever since.
